## Objective

1. Create a GitHub account
2. Get access to the Intro to Git/GitHub materials
3. Install a Git client: GitHub Desktop

## GitHub Account - Best Practices

* If you do not yet have a github account, we suggest using your personal email to set up the account so you do not lose access if you leave the WB.
* If you already have a pesonal github account, you do not need to create a second account (unless having separate accounts is your personal preference).
* You can associate multiple email addresses with your GitHub account and configure notification emails accordingly.
  * For example, use WB email address for notifications for WB-hosted repositories and personal email for other notifications.

## GitHub Account

_Skip this slide if you already have a GitHub account_

* If you do not already have a GitHub account, follow [these best-practice instructions](https://github.com/worldbank/dime-github-trainings/blob/master/GitHub-resources/DIME-GitHub-Guides/Creating-GitHub-account.md) to sign up.
* If you already have a GitHub account, use it for work as well. You are not required to create a second account.

## Repository Access

* This morning we will use this repository for the training: https://github.com/dime-wb-trainings/lyrics-aibc. It is a `public` repository, meaning that everyone can view it, but only collaborators with permission can make changes to it.
* You need to be invited to this repository with `write` access to participate in the next session. To do so:
  * Share your username with the Impact Analytics team
  * Accept the invitation to the training repository, either through the invitation link sent by GitHub or at https://github.com/dime-wb-trainings/lyrics-aibc/invitations. Wait until someone has had time to invite you before checking the invitations page.

If you are waiting to be invited, feel free to skip to the next slide and return once you have received the invitation. You do not need `write` access to complete the steps on the next slide.

## GitHub Desktop - Introduction

* You will need access to a Git client during the next session. You will also be introduced to Git clients if you are not familiar with what they are.

* There are many Git clients available, but for this training, we will use GitHub Desktop. It is a free Git client developed by GitHub and provides simplified connections between GitHub.com on the internet and GitHub Desktop on your computer.

* You may use a different Git client, but our instructions and support will focus on GitHub Desktop. If you have only used Git from the command line, we encourage you to try a graphical Git client during this training and see how it can support quality control.

Depending on whether you are using a WB computer or a personal computer, follow the relevant instructions on the next slides.

## GitHub Desktop - WB Computer

1. Install the GitHub Desktop application: Open *Software Center* from the Windows Start menu, search for **GitHub Desktop**, and click **Install**.
2. After installing GitHub Desktop, open it and go to *File* → *Options*, then log in using your GitHub account.
3. *Optional but recommended*: Go to *Help* → *About GitHub Desktop* to check for updates. GitHub Desktop will update itself automatically when a newer version is available.

For WB computers, even when you use Software Center, ITS appreciates it if you record the installation with a Software Installation request. This helps ITS understand demand and allocate resources to support GitHub Desktop.

## GitHub Desktop - Personal Computer

1. Install the GitHub Desktop application. It is a free GitHub client, and we use it in this training because it is beginner-friendly. [Download GitHub Desktop here](https://desktop.github.com/) and follow installation instructions.
2. After installing GitHub Desktop, open it and go to *File* → *Options*, then log in using your GitHub account.
3. *Optional but recommended*: Go to *Help* → *About GitHub Desktop* to check for updates. GitHub Desktop will update itself automatically when a newer version is available.
  

## Objective

You are done when the following objectives are completed:

1. Create a GitHub account
2. Get access to the Intro to Git/GitHub materials
3. Install a Git client: GitHub Desktop
